solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Literary genre in terrific story briefly recalled?

definitions.text: Literary genre in terrific story briefly recalled?

parts.words: Literary genre in terrific story briefly recalled?
parts.note: the short name of the genre sits backwards inside the words terrific story, and briefly says that short name stands for the full two-word answer

explanation.surface: Someone recalls, in a few words, the genre of a terrific story they once read.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'terrIFIC Story' backwards ('recalled') and you get SCIFI; 'briefly' says that is the short form, so the entry is the full term it abbreviates. The wordplay builds only the abbreviation, so it is treated as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories of future technology and space travel make up a familiar literary genre, commonly shortened to sci-fi.

clue.text: A dodgy dealer?

parts.note: a dealer can be a crooked businessman, but here it is the person dealing the cards at the table who cheats

explanation.surface: A shady trader, perhaps a market spiv.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealer' suggests trade; the question mark points to the one who deals cards, and a dishonest one is a cheat at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat who wins at cards by trickery is exactly a dishonest dealer of the pack.

clue.text: Looking at investment of money in grants

indicators.note: investment is a covering or enclosing, so the letters are found wrapped up inside the words money in grants

explanation.surface: Someone is studying how money is invested in grants.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something is looking at it closely; this spelling drops the middle E.

clue.text: Nation source of drug, big name I imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the star and the I are placed inside the plant's name

parts.note: coca is the plant whose leaves yield cocaine
a star is a celebrity, a big name

explanation.surface: A country that supplies drugs has taken in some famous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic between Nicaragua and Panama is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Bird finds worm under calf's bottom

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another is written after it
the bottom of the calf here means the final letter of that word, its tail end

parts.note: to worm is to inch, moving slowly along

explanation.surface: A bird finds a worm beneath a calf's hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link word. In this down clue 'under' puts INCH below F.
explanation.definitionFit: A small seed-eating songbird such as the chaffinch or goldfinch.

clue.text: Person settling close in, or abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between settling near home or overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist sets up home in a new territory, so this is a settler.

clue.text: Opening notes, interviewer needing to review objectives, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: Notes for an interviewer, who must review the objectives before starting.
explanation.definitionFit: The first bars of a piece of music, an introduction, are its opening notes.

clue.text: Bowler aims to hit one over square leg

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece over another is written before it

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler aims to have a batsman caught at square leg, a fielding position beside the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, but the bowler is at a skittle alley. 'over' sets NINE above PIN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles or tenpin bowling the player rolls the ball to knock down the standing wooden pins.

clue.text: Duck kept by old, old Briton for cat

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the duck sits within the ancient Briton

parts.note: the Celts were the early inhabitants of Britain
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton kept a duck, and then went hunting for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' puts O inside CELT, after the O for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted wild feline of Central and South America is a medium-sized cat.

clue.text: One after fish bones

indicators.note: after means the one comes behind the fish in the answer

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone after a fish that is full of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpal bones form the wrist; carpi is the Latin plural of carpus.

clue.text: One in a suit — wearing vest?

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
something you have on, you are wearing

explanation.surface: A man in a suit asks whether to wear a vest beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a suit of cards, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a lone card held in a suit is the only one of that suit in the hand.

clue.text: A dip covered in lemon rind on a dish

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped up within, so these letters sit inside the outer letters
the rind is the outer skin of the lemon, its first and last letters

parts.note: to sag is to dip or droop

explanation.surface: A dip covered in lemon peel, served on a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian baked pasta of layered sheets, meat sauce and cheese is a dish.

clue.text: Cook once stuffing spring chickens in here

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so the cooked letters are packed inside the spring

parts.note: a hop is a spring or small jump

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook once stuffed spring chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'spring chickens' look like young birds being stuffed; 'spring' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickens are housed in a coop, a hutch or pen for poultry.

clue.text: Sound of plucking pheasant now gonna mean crowing ends

indicators.note: ends means the final letters, here of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone plucking a pheasant hears it crow its last.
explanation.walkthrough: The plucking is of strings, not feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The resonant note of a plucked guitar or bow string is called by that name.

clue.text: Not entirely happy Welshman in historical county

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is left incomplete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: glad means happy
Morgan is a common Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Welshman who is not fully happy in his old home county.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAD loses its last letter by 'Not entirely'. The answer is a former county of south Wales, around Cardiff and Swansea.
explanation.definitionFit: This former county of south Wales was abolished in 1974 and survives only historically.

clue.text: Hot Finnish sauna ultimately designed to inspire love

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the love letter is taken inside the rearranged letters
designed means arranged anew, so these letters are reordered
ultimately means at the end, the last letter of sauna

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Finnish sauna, built at last, designed to inspire love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges FINNISH plus A, the final letter picked by 'ultimately', into INFASHIN, and 'to inspire' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hot is popular and currently fashionable, the latest trend.

clue.text: Father and a bird most of all related

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as the word all

explanation.surface: A father and a bird, of all creatures, turn out to be related.
explanation.definitionFit: Brotherly ties are family ties, so the adjective describes people who are related as brothers.

clue.text: Front part of shoe nicked, oddly

parts.note: the insole is the inner sole of a shoe

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: The front of someone's shoe has been oddly cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front' looks like a part of the shoe, but is the definition, meaning cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Front means brazen nerve or cheek, so it is a synonym for rude impudence.

clue.text: Leader has to lead a fool

parts.note: taken as the word to
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a nana is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone who must lead a fool around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the boss or most important person in a group is its leader.

clue.text: Departing after second lecture

indicators.note: after puts the departing word behind the second one

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
off means leaving, going away

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after the second lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or reprimand someone is to lecture them sharply.

clue.text: Part of step is elevated, initially, between rivers

indicators.note: between means placed inside, the two rivers on either side

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, twice over

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word elevated

explanation.surface: A step lies between two rivers and is raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical face of each stair, between the treads, is called by this name.

clue.text: Spirit suppressed by newspaper, on the warpath

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down inside, so the spirit is enclosed by the newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A story about a strong drink is suppressed by a newspaper, which is on the warpath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the warpath is furious, in a violent temper.

clue.text: Challenge a Liberal in power

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so a Liberal goes inside power

parts.note: clout is influence or power

explanation.surface: A Liberal in government is challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone out is to challenge them, as to a duel or over wrongdoing.

clue.text: Pick up (literally) a king penguin, finally

parts.note: Lear is a king, the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word penguin

explanation.surface: A child literally picks up a king penguin.
explanation.walkthrough: '(literally)' hints that 'a king' is a named king, Lear, not R.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or a fact is to acquire knowledge of it.

clue.text: All together expressing disapproval, no good avoiding it

indicators.note: avoiding it means keeping out of the word just given, so those letters are removed

parts.note: tutting is clicking the tongue to show disapproval

explanation.surface: Everyone together tutting at something useless.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian marking tells all the performers to play together.

clue.text: Silencer that's soft put in pair of listeners?

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the soft letter goes between the two words for ears

parts.note: an ear and a lug, a slang word for ear, make two listeners
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A silencer that's soft is put in a pair of ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear deadens noise, so it acts as a silencer.

clue.text: Religious teacher, brothers' father dismissing Old Testament in religious instruction

indicators.note: in means placed inside religious instruction

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the Old Testament letters are dropped

parts.note: an abbot is the father of monks, who are brothers

explanation.surface: A religious teacher dismisses the Old Testament from a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Monks are brothers, and the head of an abbey is their father.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish scholar and teacher of the law holds this title.

clue.text: Blooming cages chimed with an ape

indicators.note: with means alongside, so an follows the rest
cages means encloses, so the blooming word holds the chimed one

parts.note: flowers that are out are blooming
rang means chimed

explanation.surface: Bells chime in flowering cages holding an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra is a primate.

clue.text: Mountain surrounded by country

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
something hemmed in is surrounded

explanation.surface: A mountain surrounded by a country.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African nation lies between Togo and Nigeria.

clue.text: Crime not taking the newspaper

parts.note: a crime word for stealing, without its three-letter article, leaves a two-letter short name for the newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone avoids buying a paper as if it were a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: THEFT is a crime; take away 'the' and FT remains, the usual short name for the newspaper. The wordplay builds only the abbreviation, so it is treated as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink London business daily, the paper that publishes this puzzle, is known by these two letters.
